title: NPC head portraits and bestiary thumbnails (Blender render pass)
player_outcome: Housing banners, the Guide book's NPC tab and bestiary lists show proper head portraits and creature thumbnails instead of text.
design: New tools/blender/bgen/portraits.py and a build_all.py option '--portraits [--only=GLOB]'. It imports an existing GLB from assets/models/creatures (no mesh rebuild), frames it with an orthographic camera (humanoids: the 'head' bone bounds plus a margin, 3/4 view; others: the whole-body bounds), renders with Eevee/Workbench and a transparent background at 128 px, and adds a 2 px dark outline in post (PIL) for the Terraria look.
Outputs: assets/icons/npcs/<town npc id>.png (29 + pets + visitors) and assets/icons/creatures/<enemy id>.png (about 229).
Core AssetPaths: TownNpcHead(def) and CreatureIcon(enemy). The validator reports a missing portrait as a warning (ctx.Asset style), and build_all.py --check verifies coverage.
Game: new game/Items/PortraitIcons.cs with a lazy texture cache (like ItemIcons) and a threaded preload helper, LoadThreadedRequest with a per-frame budget.
tests: AssetCoverageTests: every town NPC has a head portrait
verification: Render the set; spot-check contact sheets; Godot import has no errors
risks: Rendering about 260 portraits takes minutes; shard like --anims.
Humanoid head-bone framing must match the 52-bone rig naming.
